newsitem.title: CHINA: SWIMMING-CHINA SAYS ANTI-DOPING RULES MUCH TIGHTER.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-CHINA SAYS ANTI-DOPING RULES MUCH TIGHTER.

text.p: China has tightened controls to prevent doping in swimming again this year, making the penalties even harsher for athletes who test positive, a Chinese swimming official said on Wednesday.
"We have strengthened the anti-doping campaign this year," said the official of the China Swimming Team.

"If two swimmers from any single province test positive, then the whole provincial team will be banned from taking part in the Eighth National Games this year," he said. "Any swimmer who tests positive will be banned for four years."
"No one would dare to use drugs now because the penalties are so severe," he said.

Four Chinese swimmers were banned for two years following positive dope tests at the national championships in January last year, Cornel Marculescu, director of the world governing body FINA, said in Lausanne on Tuesday.
Last year, women swimmers Yu Ran, Pu Shi and Chen Jialin tested positive for an anabolic steroid while male swimmer Lu Qiang had an illegally high ratio of testosterone to epitestosterone.

Seven Chinese tested positive for anabolic steroids at the 1994 Asian Games a month after the world championships in Rome. World champions Yang Aihua and Lu Bin were among those suspended for two years.
